If the objective is to retain the existing exposure while the missing comparison inputs are gathered, no change is needed; the snapshot stays as submitted and the modeling shows the current mark above the base case, which is a reason for caution rather than a basis for action.

answers.downside: The failure mechanism is twofold. Operationally, if AI and cloud spending normalizes, pricing pressure builds, or capital expenditure stays elevated relative to revenue, free-cash-flow conversion stays weak and the modeled values fall well short of the current mark. Structurally, the position is the overwhelming majority of the taxable account, so a single-company disappointment drives the whole portfolio; the fund and cash paths could not be modeled, so any claim that they would do better is unsupported here.

company_cases.mid_cycle_context: Cyclicality is unknown, so a mid-cycle rather than peak level is used. Reported FY2026 net margin of about forty percent was flattered by discrete items in the earnings release (an investment gain and lower voluntary-retirement costs), and non-GAAP net income was lower than GAAP, so the reported year is treated as a strong but not peak operating level. Free-cash-flow margin fell across the three reported years as capital spending rose, so the first modeled year's free-cash-flow margin is set near, not above, the latest reported ratio. Margin paths therefore sit around the reported level rather than extrapolating the best reported year.
Microsoft's cloud growth is in a mid-cycle phase, neither peak nor trough, based on historical adoption patterns of enterprise software.
